title: The essence of citizenship
competency: Describe what a citizen is, the rights and responsibilities of citizens, and the difference between citizen and citizenship.

keywords.def: A person who has specific rights and responsibilities under the law.
Full and responsible membership of the state. It is a legal status and an identity.
Something the law allows and protects for you, like expressing yourself.
A duty you must carry out, like obeying the law and paying taxes.

en.text: A citizen is a person who has specific rights and responsibilities under the law. The state gives citizens rights and benefits. In exchange, citizens follow the rules and defend their country. Ethiopian citizens may express themselves and are protected by the law. They must obey the law and pay taxes.

screens.title: The unit picture
screens.ask: Your passport says "Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia". What does it show about you?
opts: That you are a member of the Ethiopian state
That you are a good student
That you can travel for free
screens.after: A passport shows that the state recognises you as its member. That membership is called citizenship. Read on.

screens.title: Unit 1 Citizenship
paras: In lower grades you learned about moral education and the values of a good citizen.
This unit covers citizenship, its essence and the features of good citizenship.
It also shows how a person gets and loses citizenship, and Ethiopian citizenship law.

screens.title: 1.1.1 The essence of citizenship
paras: A citizen is a person who has specific rights and responsibilities under the law.
The state gives citizens specific rights and benefits.
In exchange, citizens follow their country's rules and defend it against its enemies.

screens.title: Rights and responsibilities
screens.ask: Tap each one. Is it a right or a responsibility?
items: A right: Ethiopian citizens may express themselves.
A right: the law protects every citizen.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A person who has specific rights and responsibilities under the law.
Something the law allows and protects for you.
A duty you must carry out, like obeying the law.

opts: A person who has rights but no duties
A person who has specific rights and responsibilities under the law
A person who works for the government
screens.ans: A person who has specific rights and responsibilities under the law
screens.why: A citizen has both rights and responsibilities under the law.
screens.clue: A citizen gets something and also gives something.

screens.title: Right or responsibility?
items: To be protected by the law
To defend the country against its enemies
screens.why: Rights are what you receive; responsibilities are what you must do.
screens.clue: Ask: is this something I get, or something I must do?

screens.text: Citizens are expected to follow their country's rules and defend it against its enemies.
screens.why: The book says citizens do this in exchange for their rights.
screens.clue: What do citizens give back for their rights?

screens.text: Kebede says: "I am a citizen, so I have rights. I do not need to pay taxes." What is wrong?
opts: A citizen has responsibilities too, such as paying taxes
Taxes are a right, not a duty
screens.ans: A citizen has responsibilities too, such as paying taxes
screens.why: Citizenship gives rights AND responsibilities. Paying taxes is one of the responsibilities.
screens.clue: A citizen has two kinds of things. Kebede forgot one.

en.text: Citizenship is full and responsible membership of the state. The member has a duty to the state, and the state must protect the member. So citizenship is both a legal status and an identity. A citizen is the person; citizenship is the membership that person holds.

screens.title: Two words
screens.ask: Is there any difference between "citizen" and "citizenship"?
opts: Yes: one is a person, the other is a membership
Yes: citizenship is only for adults
screens.after: A citizen is a person. Citizenship is the membership or status the person holds. Read on.

screens.title: Citizenship
paras: Citizenship refers to full and responsible membership of the state.
Members have a duty to the state. The state must protect its members.
Therefore, citizenship is a legal status and an identity.
screens.note: Remember: citizenship is both a legal status and a sense of identity.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Full and responsible membership of the state; a legal status and an identity.

screens.text: Citizenship is both a legal status and ___.
screens.why: The book says citizenship is a legal status and an identity.
Citizen and state each owe something to the other.
screens.clue: Who is the person, and what is the membership?

screens.text: In citizenship, only the citizen has duties; the state has none.
screens.why: The state has an obligation to protect its members.
screens.clue: Read the sentence about the state's obligation.

screens.text: Which sentence uses both words correctly?
opts: Almaz is a citizenship of Ethiopia
Almaz is a citizen; she holds Ethiopian citizenship
screens.ans: Almaz is a citizen; she holds Ethiopian citizenship
screens.why: A citizen is the person (Almaz). Citizenship is the membership she holds.

ideas.name: Case study: two children and school

en.text: In the case study, parents keep their children home to help with work. But going to school is the children's own right as citizens, protected by the law. It does not depend only on their parents' goodwill. Children can learn and still help at home.

screens.title: Help at home or school?
screens.ask: Parents want their children to stay home and help with daily work instead of going to school. Is this a good reason?
opts: No, school is the children's right
screens.after: Going to school is a child's right. The case study asks you to think about it.

screens.title: Case study
paras: In a small village there were two children. They helped their parents and were well liked.
Teachers asked the parents to send the children to school next year.
The parents refused. They wanted the children to keep helping with daily work.

screens.title: Key word
defs: Something the law allows and protects for you.

screens.text: Does a child's right to attend school depend only on the parents' goodwill?
opts: No, it is the child's right, protected by law
Only if the school is near
screens.ans: No, it is the child's right, protected by law
screens.why: Citizens have rights under the law. The state must protect them. A right is not just a favour from parents.

screens.text: How convincing is the parents' reason?
opts: Not convincing: the children can learn and still help at home
screens.ans: Not convincing: the children can learn and still help at home
screens.why: Wanting help with work does not outweigh the right to education.

screens.text: Which are rights or duties of the children? Tap all that fit.
pool: To be protected by the law
a: To be protected by the law
screens.why: They have the right to school and protection, and duties to learn and to respect parents and teachers.
screens.clue: One option takes away a right.

screens.text: What is the best ending for the story?
opts: The children never go to school
The teachers and community help the parents agree; the children go to school and help after class
screens.ans: The teachers and community help the parents agree; the children go to school and help after class
screens.why: This protects the children's right to education and still helps the family.
screens.clue: Look for the answer that respects both school and family.

items.text: What do we mean by citizenship?
opts: Full and responsible membership of the state
items.ans: Full and responsible membership of the state
items.why: Citizenship is full and responsible membership of the state.
items.clue: Think about being a member of the state.

items.text: Is there any difference between citizen and citizenship?
opts: Yes: a citizen is the person, citizenship is the membership or status
items.ans: Yes: a citizen is the person, citizenship is the membership or status
items.why: One word names the person, the other names the status.

test.text: A citizen is a person who has ___ under the law.
test.why: A citizen has both rights and responsibilities.

test.text: Citizenship is a legal status and an identity.
test.why: The book says this in the Remember box.

test.text: Which is a responsibility of an Ethiopian citizen?
opts: To be protected by the law
test.why: Paying taxes is a duty. The others are rights or benefits.

test.text: What does the state owe its members?
test.why: The state has an obligation of protection to the member.

test.text: A girl's parents keep her home to sell goods. Which idea from this lesson helps her most?
opts: Going to school is her right as a citizen, protected by law
test.ans: Going to school is her right as a citizen, protected by law
test.why: Her right to education is protected by law and does not depend only on her parents.

notes.text: The book also says "a citizen is someone who has the right to be called a citizen" (p.4 text and Remember box). This is circular, so the lesson uses the book's first definition: a person with specific rights and responsibilities under the law.
Case study Q1 and Q4 are open questions; they are asked as multiple choice with a book-based model answer.
1.1 has only an intro and two start-up questions; they are placed here as an exercise.
